Audio Priority Bar 2.8.0 shows a Jabra headset's battery on its Link dongle, can mute the speakers when your headphones disconnect, and tidies the panel and the menu bar icon. Coming from 2.7.0, the update installs in place, and your existing priorities and overrides are kept.

## Devices

- A Jabra headset behind a Link dongle shows its battery level on the dongle's rows, orange at 20% or below ([#34](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/34)).
- A new **Mute speakers when headphones disconnect** option in Settings, off by default, mutes the speakers when the headphones playing disconnect, are turned off or run out of battery. Falling back to other headphones stays audible ([#33](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/33)).

## Menu bar

- With the microphone shown, a headset whose mic belongs to the output, such as AirPods or a USB headset, appears once instead of twice. A muted microphone still appears beside it, and the labeled icon keeps both ([#31](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/31)).

## Panel

- A row's selection override and actions menu appear on hover, with VoiceOver on, or with keyboard focus, and right-clicking a row opens the same menu. The footer is tidied and Settings gets a gear icon ([#32](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/32), contribution by [Dave Smith](https://github.com/djsmith42)).
- **Show Device** is renamed **Unhide Device**, to read as the reverse of **Hide Device** ([#29](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/29), contribution by [Dave Smith](https://github.com/djsmith42)).

## Thanks

Thanks to @djsmith42, who contributed two more pull requests to this release.

## Install

```bash
brew install --cask camguillory/tap/audio-priority-bar
```

Alternatively, download `AudioPriorityBar.zip` and `AudioPriorityBar.zip.sha256` below into the same folder, verify the archive, and move the app to `/Applications`:

```bash
shasum -a 256 -c AudioPriorityBar.zip.sha256
```

The release is universal for Apple silicon and Intel. It is signed with the project's own certificate, not an Apple Developer ID, and not notarized. If macOS blocks the first launch, open **System Settings > Privacy & Security** and click **Open Anyway**.

Jabra Link monitoring may request Input Monitoring permission. Link 380 is hardware-verified. Link 390 is expected to work through the same capability check but remains unverified on hardware, and monitoring fails open when the link state cannot be read.
